description: Shared cross-trait behavioral signal library for interview evaluation

signals.label: Explicitly names or labels a child’s emotion using clear feeling language
Accurately interprets the cause or context of a child’s emotional state
Mislabels or oversimplifies a child’s emotional experience
Uses co-regulation strategies such as calm presence, soothing voice, or proximity
Uses soothing techniques such as tone, rhythm, or gentle touch
Relies on distraction as the primary strategy instead of addressing underlying needs
Validates the child’s feelings verbally or behaviorally
Minimizes, dismisses, or invalidates a child’s feelings
Speaks about children or others in a respectful and non-judgmental way
Uses negative or judgmental labels to describe a child or person
Frames situation from the child’s perspective
Frames situation primarily around adult needs or compliance
Recognizes their own emotional state or stress signals
Uses intentional strategies to regulate themselves
Maintains calm tone and body language under stress
Escalates tone, behavior, or emotional intensity
Adjusts approach based on feedback or child response
Remains rigid and does not adjust approach when needed
Repeats ineffective strategies without adjusting
Observes multiple behavioral or nonverbal cues
Notices subtle or nuanced cues in behavior
Takes responsibility for their role in a situation
Blames others or external factors without self-reflection
Demonstrates openness to feedback
Responds defensively to feedback
Demonstrates understanding of another person’s perspective
Speaks disrespectfully about others
Uses slow, controlled, and gentle physical handling
Handles children in a rushed, rough, or task-focused way
Adjusts actions based on child comfort or resistance
Reflects on what worked or what they learned
Shows little or no reflection on their actions
Demonstrates openness to growth and improvement
Demonstrates resistance to change or improvement
Balances empathy with appropriate boundaries and limits
Balances flexibility with needed structure and consistency
Balances an individual child’s needs with the needs of the group
Balances task efficiency with relational care and connection
Explains a clear, structured response process
Describes an observe-respond-reassess loop or similar iterative process
Describes actions vaguely without a clear process
Makes the reasoning behind actions explicit
Evaluates whether the chosen strategy worked
Links decisions to child development, learning, or developmental appropriateness
